# Yes MCP

> Model Context Protocol engineering for companies: custom servers over internal and
> legacy systems, security and authorisation review, readiness for the 2026-07-28
> specification, and interactive UI (MCP Apps) inside the assistant.

Notes are written from a server that runs in production, not from the specification.
Every number published here was measured on a real system and is dated.

## Writing

- [The MCP spec shipped one day after its SDK](https://yesmcp.com/writing/spec-shipped-after-its-sdk/): the 2026-07-28 stateless rewrite started a twelve-month migration clock; the TypeScript SDK was published 2026-07-27 and supports protocol versions only up to 2025-11-25, so the migration cannot be executed yet.
- [Your tool results are being read as an attack](https://yesmcp.com/writing/tool-results-read-as-injection/): imperative instructions inside a tool result match the tool-poisoning signature; a host warned a real user about our own connector. How we split the channels, and what it saved (frame 1043 → 509 characters, ~130 tokens per call).
- [What the host doesn't deliver](https://yesmcp.com/writing/what-the-host-does-not-deliver/): the server `instructions` field never reaches the model; a deferred tool's description is unreachable until the tool loads; a new MCP session opens on nearly every call; the tool list is re-sent before every call (5698 bytes).

## About

- [Serhii Kravchenko ,  MCP engineer](https://yesmcp.com/about/): who runs this, what has been built and verified (a production MCP server with OAuth 2.1 serving a live user through Claude on web, mobile and desktop; MCP Apps views rendering with real data), and how these notes are produced. No client case studies are claimed.
